geo.label: Lift-off priced; curve bear-flattening
parts: Macro Stance

The US enters February with growth strong enough to validate lift-off and a market arguing about speed. Al Jazeera reports the economy added 467,000 jobs in January, calming Omicron fears [[n2074]], and Reuters describes a labour market that shrugged off the Omicron surge with the economy strong ahead of rate hikes [[n2073]]. That follows an ISM manufacturing PMI of 57.6 index points [[n2028]], a December in which job openings exceeded unemployed workers by 4.6 million, per CNBC [[n2035]], and fourth-quarter GDP growth of 6.9%, per The Real Economy Blog [[n2005]]. The stance is Mixed, not Bullish, because that strength removes the Fed's reason to wait: the policy put has been struck lower, and equity multiples rather than earnings are carrying the adjustment.
Rates & Curve

The 2Y Treasury closed at 1.31% and the 10Y at 1.93%, leaving 10Y-2Y at +62 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-04). Over 20 observations the 2Y rose 43 bps from 0.88% while the 10Y rose 20 bps from 1.73%, so the spread narrowed 23 bps: a bear flattening, in a curve that is still moderately steep. The move accelerated last week, with the 2Y up 16 bps and the 10Y up 15 bps over five observations. Reuters explains why the flattening matters [[n2113]], Standard Chartered expects the curve to flatten and possibly invert this year [[n2099]], and Credit Suisse warns an inversion may be a false-positive recession signal [[n2121]]. Tipswatch notes the 30-year real yield has risen above zero [[n2147]], removing the negative real-rate subsidy beneath long-duration equity.
New / Most Important

The swing factor is pace, not direction. Reuters argues the Fed is unlikely to start hiking with a bang [[n2139]], whereas the Fed's Bullard sees three successive hikes to start tightening [[n2104]]. Equities absorbed the jobs data: the S&P 500 closed at 4,500.53 index points, +1.55% over five sessions but -4.16% over 20, and the Nasdaq 100 rose +1.66% on the week to 14,694.35 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). VIX eased to 23.22 index points, -16.05% over five sessions, and the dollar index (DXY) fell -1.84% to 95.48 index points. Fiscal support is fading, with PBS reporting Manchin says Build Back Better is dead [[n2108]], and Fed leadership is in limbo: Reuters reports Powell will serve as chair pro tempore as he awaits Senate action [[n2138]].
Playbook ✓

Action: stay underweight front-end duration and unprofitable long-duration growth; prefer cash-generative mega-caps, energy and money-centre banks that monetise a higher 2Y. Trigger: the 2Y holding at or above 1.31% while 10Y-2Y compresses further from +62 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-04) confirms the bear-flattening regime. What changes the call: a soft next CPI print or a bond rally that drags the 2Y back toward the 0.88% of 20 observations ago would show the hiking path is over-priced; rotating back into quality growth such as the Nasdaq 100, still -6.79% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), would then offer the better risk-reward. A VIX spike that reverses last week's -16.05% decline would argue for cutting gross exposure first.

geo.label: ECB pivot risk; energy squeeze
parts: Macro Stance

Europe faces a hawkish pivot without the growth momentum to absorb it. DW reports the ECB kept rates on hold [[n1245]], but Al Jazeera says Lagarde is no longer ruling out a hike this year [[n0100]], and the Bank of England raised rates with four officials wanting more, per Reuters [[n1244]]. European equities lagged the US: the Euro Stoxx 50 closed at 4,086.58 index points, -1.22% over five sessions, and the DAX fell -1.75% on Friday to 15,099.56 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04).
Activity & Inflation

Inflation is the binding constraint. Bankier.pl notes euro-area inflation surprised economists again [[n1621]], and BNP Paribas flags an unusual gap between French and German inflation [[n1223]]. Energy is the transmission channel: Reuters catalogues Europe's efforts to shield households from soaring energy costs [[n1248]], while the New York Times reports gas shipments, mostly from the US, are easing the crunch [[n1491]]. Dutch TTF gas closed at 82.65 EUR/MWh, -10.22% over five sessions and -14.35% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), relief that stays fragile while Bloomberg sets out two ways a war in Ukraine would hit Europe's gas [[n1216]]. Intereconomics asks how large the stagflation risk is [[n1260]].
New / Most Important

Repricing hit rate-sensitive exporters hardest: SAP is -9.98% over 20 sessions to 109.18 EUR and Siemens -12.70% to 132.84 EUR, while Societe Generale rose +3.62% over five sessions to 34.03 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Banks are the cleanest beneficiary of an ECB that can no longer promise zero rates for the year.
Playbook ✓

Action: own euro-area banks against German industrial and software exporters. Trigger: hawkish ECB language confirmed while TTF stays at or below 82.65 EUR/MWh (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04) keeps the bank-over-industrial spread working. What changes the call: a renewed gas spike on a Ukraine escalation, which would hit bank asset quality through energy-intensive borrowers and reverse the trade.

geo.label: Easing bias meets weak activity
parts: Macro Stance

China comes back from the Lunar New Year with policy leaning against a slowing economy. Mainland shares have not traded since the Shanghai Composite closed at 3,361.44 index points, -4.57% over five sessions and -7.12% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-28), so onshore prices still embed pre-holiday pessimism. Hong Kong reopened more constructively: the Hang Seng closed at 24,573.29 index points, +3.24% from its last pre-holiday session and +5.51% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). The stance is Mixed. Bloomberg says the central bank is seizing the moment for stimulus as the Fed hikes [[n0140]], yet CNN reports George Soros warning that China is facing an economic crisis [[n0156]].
PMIs & Activity

Activity going into the holiday was soft. Reuters reports January factory activity contracted on the Caixin measure as COVID lockdowns bit [[n0145]], Hürriyet Daily News says official factory activity edged down [[n0152]], and ABN AMRO concludes the January PMIs indicate quarter-on-quarter growth will drop in Q1 [[n0150]]. The base is demanding: Global Times reports GDP grew 8.1% in 2021, the fastest in a decade [[n0129]], with fixed-asset investment up 4.9%, per Macau Business [[n0131]]. Geopolitical Futures ties zero-COVID to manufacturing risk [[n0241]], and HSBC tells CNBC that disruptions in China can ripple across global supply chains [[n0155]]. The Caixin services survey still to come is the next test of whether Omicron curbs are spreading from factories to consumers.
Credit Impulse

Monetary policy has clearly turned. CNBC reports the central bank cut key lending rates, including one for the first time in nearly two years [[n0135]], after the BBC reported rate cuts as growth slowed [[n0128]]; Fibre2Fashion details the cuts to medium-term loans and reverse repos [[n0138]]. The direction is unambiguous but transmission is not: cuts lower the price of credit, while developers' balance-sheet stress limits demand for it. BNP Paribas Asset Management argues China's debt vulnerability keeps defying dire predictions [[n0223]], a reminder that the state-bank system can absorb losses while growth slows. The credit impulse should turn up from policy, but with a lag that keeps the first quarter weak and leaves equities trading the promise rather than the data.
Property

Property remains the drag. Caixin Global reports the property market made a bleak start to 2022 [[n0184]], and Business Recorder says December new home prices fell less only because of promotions and easing curbs [[n0126]]. Reuters describes dashed dreams at China Evergrande's showpiece resort island [[n0159]], and The Real Deal reports Oaktree Capital has seized a second Evergrande property [[n0175]], evidence that creditors are enforcing rather than waiting for a rescue. Until sales stabilise, developers cut land purchases, local governments lose land revenue and the steel chain stays weak; Reuters notes 2021 iron ore imports retreated from a record on steel curbs [[n0123]].
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Beijing's mix combines easing with control. The WSJ describes Xi Jinping's push to scale China's three big mountains under common prosperity [[n0208]], and the South China Morning Post reports JD.com's founder donating US$2 billion to charity amid the tech crackdown [[n0202]]. Trade friction persists: Reuters reports a US trade official says China failed to meet Phase 1 commitments [[n0179]], while PBS reports the House passed a bill to boost US chip production to compete with China [[n0233]]. The external pivot is toward Moscow: Reuters reports Russia and China agreed a 30-year gas deal via a new pipeline, to settle in euros [[n0767]], and Putin hailed $117.5 bln of China deals [[n0808]]. The BBC says China joined Russia in opposing NATO expansion [[n1388]], which raises secondary-sanction risk for Chinese banks and exporters.
Markets & Flows

Offshore China has been the relative winner. FXI closed at 37.98 USD, +4.92% over five sessions, KWEB at 36.44 USD, +6.89%, and Alibaba's US ADR at 122.22 USD, +6.07%, while ASHR, the onshore CSI 300 tracker, gained only +1.56% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). In Hong Kong, Tencent closed at 454.94 HKD, +9.67% over 20 sessions, and Alibaba rose +4.97% to 120.40 HKD on reopening. EV ADRs led: Li Auto rose +19.73% over five sessions, XPeng +15.86% and NIO +14.64%. CnEVPost reports China accounted for 53% of global passenger NEV sales in 2021 [[n0244]], and the South China Morning Post says sales surged at Xpeng, Li Auto and NIO [[n0454]]. The gap between offshore gains and the stale onshore close is the immediate reopening risk.
New / Most Important

Geopolitics has moved ahead of data. CBS News reports the Beijing Winter Olympics opened under a cloud of controversy [[n0216]], and DW says Russia and China criticised NATO after Putin and Xi's talks [[n1392]]; Al Jazeera notes Taiwan condemned the contemptible timing of the partnership [[n1409]]. For investors the practical question is whether Beijing becomes Russia's sanctions buffer. Reuters reports Rosneft agreed a 100 mln T oil supply deal with CNPC [[n0814]], deepening exactly the energy ties that Western sanctions would target. That widens the tail risk for state banks and commodity traders even as domestic easing supports equities.
Playbook ✓

Action: stay long offshore China internet and EV exposure (KWEB, Alibaba, Li Auto) sized for volatility, and avoid property-linked credit. Trigger: a mainland reopening that narrows the gap between the Shanghai Composite's stale close of 3,361.44 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-28) and Hong Kong's +3.24% reopening gain, plus further central-bank easing, would confirm the policy-led rebound. What changes the call: a weak services survey, a fresh developer default, or US secondary sanctions on Chinese entities over Russia. ⚠ Divergence: policy is easing and offshore prices are rising, yet the Caixin factory gauge is contracting [[n0145]], the property market made a bleak start to the year [[n0184]] and the onshore market fell -7.12% over 20 sessions into the holiday; the rally is pricing policy, not activity.

geo.label: BOJ anchored; imported cost squeeze
parts: Macro Stance

Japan faces less monetary-policy pressure than the US, UK or euro area, but heavy imported cost pressure. Reuters reported the BOJ debating how to message an eventual rate hike as inflation perks up [[n1424]], but nothing like the Fed's path is priced. The Nikkei 225 closed at 27,439.99 index points, +2.70% over five sessions but -3.68% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), outperforming Europe as chip-equipment names rebounded: Tokyo Electron rose +5.80% to 56,040.00 JPY and Advantest +3.38% to 9,480.00 JPY. SoftBank Group gained +8.74% to 5,214.00 JPY on the growth bounce, while Toyota, at 2,277.50 JPY, is flat over 20 sessions at -0.31%.
Activity & Currency

The activity signal is mixed. PressReader reports factory output fell [[n1441]], and the Japan Times says the job market showed signs of healing before Omicron spread [[n1442]]. Trade values are inflating: Reuters reports December exports and imports hit record highs by value as supply bottlenecks eased [[n1426]]. Cost pass-through has started, with Reuters noting a Cup Noodle price hike may test student budgets [[n1459]] and utilities reeling as sky-high fuel prices hit earnings [[n1019]]. With US yields rising and the BOJ anchored, the rate differential works against the yen, raising import costs for utilities and food processors while flattering exporters' earnings. Sony shows the split: Barron's reports profits soared on Spider-Man despite PlayStation problems [[n0589]].
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer exporters and semiconductor equipment (Tokyo Electron, Advantest) over utilities and domestic food producers. Trigger: a firmer Fed path while the BOJ stays on hold widens the rate gap and keeps the yen soft. What changes the call: a BOJ signal that it will tolerate higher yields, or a global chip-capex downgrade; either would remove the currency and cycle tailwinds at the same time.

geo.label: Patient RBA under inflation pressure
parts: Macro Stance

The RBA is defending patience on rates while the data and its critics test it. Governor Philip Lowe's statement on the February decision [[n0033]] was followed by an ABC report quoting the governor that interest rates will go up and people need buffers [[n0021]]. The Statement on Monetary Policy's inflation chapter [[n0064]] lands after the AFR reported a shock inflation spike to 3.5 per cent [[n0010]], and Future Fund chair Peter Costello says the RBA's credibility is damaged, per SMH [[n0027]].
Demand & Financing

Demand is supported by jobs and housing wealth. The Australian reported the jobless rate hit a 13-year low as an RBA hike looms [[n0005]], and SMH says the median house price is above $1 million [[n0024]]. The financing risk sits in mortgages, which UNSW researchers argue are fixed for shareholders, not home owners [[n0062]]. Banks lagged: Commonwealth Bank closed at 94.10 AUD, -5.87% over 20 sessions, while miners carried the market, with Rio Tinto +13.24% to 114.61 AUD and BHP +9.68% to 41.68 AUD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). The S&P/ASX 200 closed at 7,120.20 index points, +1.89% over five sessions.
Playbook ✓

Action: favour iron-ore miners over banks and long-duration health care such as CSL, -7.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Trigger: Chinese easing that supports steel demand while the RBA holds. What changes the call: a faster RBA hiking path, which would help bank margins but threaten housing, or a renewed iron-ore slide like the drop of more than 6% in Singapore futures reported by Shanghai Metals Market [[n0032]].

geo.label: Shield versus tightening and security risk
parts: Macro Stance

Poland pairs rapid growth with inflation at its highest in 21 years, per Bankier.pl [[n1516]], and both are forcing the central bank's hand. Obserwator Gospodarczy reports GUS data showing GDP grew 5.7% in 2021 [[n1538]], while 300Gospodarka notes inflation rose to 8.6% at the end of 2021 on high food prices [[n1517]]. Registered unemployment reached 5.6% in January, according to the labour ministry as reported by RadioMaryja.pl [[n1700]]. NBP Governor Glapiński says growth will be fast despite the threat of Russian aggression against Ukraine, per Gazeta Prawna [[n1665]], but Rzeczpospolita argues a slowdown is being masked by statistics as inflation and rates already curb appetites [[n1564]]. The stance is Mixed: the domestic cycle is strong, yet real incomes, the currency and security risk all point the other way.
Markets

Equities are pricing stress. The Beta ETF WIG20TR tracker closed at 37.53 PLN, -2.70% on the day and -5.91% over 20 sessions, and EPOL, the dollar-based Poland ETF, fell -1.84% to 20.82 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Strefa Inwestorów writes that GPW investors fear a crash and crisis, which is why the Polish market is valued very low [[n1541]]. Rates are the counterweight: Pekao expects the Monetary Policy Council to raise rates by 50 bps in February, per StockWatch.pl [[n1706]], Morgan Stanley predicts a dynamic rise in Polish rates, per Strefa Inwestorów [[n1668]], and WIBOR keeps rising as banks are certain of further hikes [[n1609]]. The zloty has been the weak link, with FXMAG calling it once again the worst-performing currency [[n1587]], although Comparic reports EUR/PLN moved away from Monday's peak [[n1672]].
Fiscal & Politics

Fiscal policy is leaning against the central bank. From 1 February VAT is lower on food, energy and fuel, per Prawo.pl [[n1552]], as the government's Anti-Inflation Shield 2.0 took effect, per Gov.pl [[n1600]]. Retail pass-through looks thin: Bankier.pl calls the shelf effect penny-sized cuts [[n1622]], and Radio ESKA reports petrol-station owners are considering closures after the fuel price cut [[n1677]]. Money.pl says economists are tallying the shield's costs and revenues [[n1650]]. The Polski Ład tax reform has become a liability: Wyborcza.biz reports heads are to roll at the finance ministry [[n1633]], and Miesięcznik Finansowy BANK says experts call the law irreparable and want an entirely new act [[n1735]]. President Duda signed the 2022 budget law, per Radio Kraków [[n1643]], and submitted a bill aimed at ending the rule-of-law dispute with the EU, per Reuters [[n1493]].
Corporate & Sectors

Dispersion is wide. Banks are the rate trade: Bank Pekao closed at 134.40 PLN, +8.56% over 20 sessions, and mBank rose +5.70% over five sessions to 482.00 PLN despite a -2.59% Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Coal miner JSW is the energy-crisis winner, +11.54% over five sessions and +17.24% over 20 to 44.95 PLN, as Bankier.pl reports investors are counting on good results [[n1629]]. State-controlled energy names are under pressure: Orlen is -13.70% over 20 sessions to 68.92 PLN while Subiektywnie o finansach issues a stark warning about the Orlen-Lotos merger [[n1607]], and PGE fell -5.12% on Friday to 7.52 PLN. Consumer names are weak, with LPP -16.12% and Dino -12.68% over 20 sessions. CD Projekt is -10.45% over 20 sessions to 177.88 PLN even as StockWatch.pl reports it is concentrating on two AAA projects [[n1572]], and XTB rose after preliminary results, per Bankier.pl [[n1654]].
Geopolitics & Security

Poland is now the front line of NATO's response. Reuters reports the first US reinforcement troops have arrived with more expected [[n1502]], Notes From Poland says a preparatory group arrived ahead of the deployment of 1,700 troops [[n1501]], and Reuters reports Poland received US army equipment to bolster the eastern flank [[n1500]]. Warsaw is also arming Kyiv: Defense Express reports Poland will supply Piorun MANPADS to Ukraine [[n1489]], and Reuters reports Britain, Poland and Ukraine are in cooperation talks over the Russian threat [[n1472]]. The exposure is direct. Interia publishes satellite images under the line that Warsaw is within missile range [[n1659]], and reports Putin, alongside Orban, calling NATO's enlargement to include Poland a fraud [[n1569]]. Defence24 runs the contrarian opinion that there will be no invasion [[n1709]]; Polish asset prices are not trading that scenario.
New / Most Important

The February MPC decision is the domestic catalyst and energy bills are the political one. Business Insider Polska reports bakers facing gas price increases of up to 1000% have written to the prime minister [[n1703]], and WP Finanse says PGNiG customers are surprised by the scale of increases on new gas invoices [[n1640]]. That is the shield's blind spot: VAT relief at the pump does little for small firms' gas costs. Coface's head warns of a rise in insolvent companies, per Rzeczpospolita [[n1598]], which would land first on bank asset quality in consumer and SME books. Higher rates therefore help bank margins now but raise credit costs later.
Playbook ✓

Action: overweight Polish banks (Pekao, PKO BP) against utilities, refiners and discretionary retail (PGE, Orlen, LPP), while keeping total Poland exposure underweight and hedged. Trigger: an MPC hike of the size Pekao expects, with the WIG20TR tracker holding above 37.53 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), would confirm that the rate benefit outweighs the security discount. What changes the call: a Russian escalation that hits the zloty and Polish risk premia, or a weaker currency that forces faster hikes and tips households and SMEs into arrears. ⚠ Divergence: banks are pricing a stronger rate path while the index and the zloty are pricing a security and stagflation shock; both cannot persist for long, and a hawkish NBP strengthens the bank leg only if the currency stabilises.
Narrative

Technology bounced, but leadership narrowed to cash-rich platforms. XLK closed at 159.60 USD, +1.01% over five sessions and -4.70% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), trailing the Nasdaq 100's +1.66% as rate pressure capped multiples.
Reported

Microsoft beat on earnings and revenue with an upbeat fiscal third-quarter forecast, per CNBC [[n0969]], and Apple posted record holiday-quarter sales despite supply constraints, per CNN [[n0977]]; Apple closed at 172.39 USD, +1.21% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Intel's first-quarter forecast missed the Street, per the Fiji Times [[n0979]], and the stock is -11.11% over 20 sessions to 48.01 USD.
EPS Upside Watch

The upside sits in cloud consumption. Shacknews reports AWS revenue rose 40% in Q4 to $17.78 billion [[n0097]], validating demand for usage-billed software such as Datadog, +8.87% on Friday to 150.26 USD, and Snowflake, +7.59% to 275.72 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04); estimate upgrades are likeliest where billing scales with that spend.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The contrarian point is that Apple's privacy change, the event that hurt Meta, is a tailwind for Apple itself. The New York Times describes an Apple change tormenting internet companies, especially Meta [[n0624]]; platform owners, not app-dependent advertisers, are capturing the value.
Narrative

Communication services were the battleground: XLC closed at 71.17 USD, -1.58% over five sessions and -6.88% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), as Meta Platforms (FB), at 237.09 USD and -21.42% over five sessions, swamped gains elsewhere.
Reported

Bloomberg reports Meta erased $251 billion in value, the biggest wipeout in history [[n0685]], after Business Insider said Facebook's user numbers shrank for the first time [[n1102]]. Reuters reports Google propelled record revenue and drove Alphabet shares up 8% [[n0084]], and Snap closed at 38.91 USD, +58.82% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), its best day ever per Barron's [[n0817]].
EPS Upside Watch

Digiday reports Google, Meta and Amazon are on track to absorb more than 50% of all ad money in 2022 [[n1154]], so share shifts inside that pool matter more than its size; Alphabet's and Snap's results suggest the iOS damage is company-specific.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Reuters frames Meta's miss as a Big Tech divide over who has the data [[n1113]]; if Meta rebuilds measurement, the price discounts a long decline. Telecoms offer no shelter: AT&T is -4.48% over five sessions to 24.08 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04); CNBC reports its CEO says the dividend cut shifts cash back into the business [[n0741]].
Narrative

Financials are the cleanest expression of a bear flattening that still leaves the curve moderately steep. XLF closed at 40.10 USD, +3.56% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), as the 2Y climbed 16 bps over five observations to 1.31% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-04), lifting expected yields on banks' floating-rate assets.
Reported

Bank of America rose +5.25% over five sessions to 48.28 USD, Goldman Sachs +5.93% to 367.60 USD and JPMorgan +4.06% to 152.56 USD, while the regional bank ETF KRE gained +3.44% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Rate-sensitive Charles Schwab rose +3.39% on Friday to 91.90 USD. Reuters reports ING shares dipped 4% after earnings as provisions rose on inflation worries [[n1105]].
EPS Upside Watch

Higher front-end rates lift net interest income first at deposit-rich lenders and brokers, and that revision cycle has barely begun. The limiting factor is credit: ING's provisioning shows inflation can raise expected losses even while margins widen.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Payments, usually grouped with financial growth, are the weak link. Visa fell -1.36% and Mastercard -2.02% on Friday, and PayPal's guidance shock, which CNBC calls its worst-ever trading day [[n0580]], shows fintech now trades as long-duration technology rather than as a rate beneficiary.
Narrative

Energy leads on 20-session momentum. XLE closed at 68.90 USD, +4.98% over five sessions and +13.87% over 20, with WTI at 92.31 USD/bbl, +16.17% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Reuters reports strategists see oil hitting $100 on demand and the Russia-Ukraine crisis [[n1389]].
Reported

Reuters reports Exxon posted its biggest profit in seven years on high oil prices [[n0404]], and Shell ended 2021 on a high note, hiking its dividend and boosting buybacks [[n0710]]. Chevron kicked off the season with a miss, per Reuters [[n0986]], yet is +10.24% over 20 sessions to 135.88 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04).
EPS Upside Watch

Al Jazeera reports OPEC+ is sticking to planned output hikes despite surging prices [[n0093]], yet OPEC barely raised output last month [[n1821]]; quotas outrunning capacity support prices and upstream estimates. Occidental, +24.54% over 20 sessions to 40.80 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), has the most operating leverage.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Consensus treats energy as a war hedge; the stronger case is capital discipline. Exxon earned $23 billion in 2021 and initiated a $10 billion share repurchase [[n1291]]: buybacks, not new drilling, send higher prices to shareholders, which is why Exxon, +8.14% over five sessions, rerated early.
Narrative

Industrials split between transport and aerospace winners and supply-chain-hit capital goods. XLI closed at 100.11 USD, -1.08% on Friday, +0.41% over five sessions and -6.02% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04).
Reported

Reuters reports UPS offered a brighter view after an outstanding 2021 and its shares hit a record high [[n0474]]. Boeing rose +8.33% over five sessions to 206.45 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04) after CNBC reported a Qatar Airways order for 737 Max planes and new 777X freighters [[n0269]]. Caterpillar, which reported fourth-quarter results [[n0985]], is -10.62% over 20 sessions to 198.41 USD, and Reuters reports GE's shares fell as supply-chain woes hit Q4 revenue [[n0964]].
EPS Upside Watch

Pricing power in logistics is the upside: Supply Chain Dive says parcel shipping will be even more expensive in 2022 [[n0999]]. Aerospace adds a second leg, with Reuters reporting American Airlines will buy more 737 MAX jets [[n0504]]. Emerson beat on automation and cold-chain demand, per Reuters [[n0537]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The New York Times reports a normal supply chain is unlikely in 2022 [[n1931]]. That hurts assemblers such as Eaton, -3.72% on Friday to 151.00 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), but helps companies that sell scarcity, such as freight carriers.
Narrative

Consumer discretionary is a two-stock story plus a margin squeeze. XLY closed at 184.40 USD, +2.84% on Friday and -9.10% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), with Amazon's +13.54% surge to 3,152.79 USD doing the lifting.
Reported

Reuters calls Amazon's move a record $190 billion gain in value [[n0747]], and CNBC attributes it to a cloud revenue beat and a huge profit gain from the Rivian stake [[n0634]]. Ford fell -9.70% to 17.96 USD as its shares skidded despite a bullish 2022 outlook, per Reuters [[n0661]], and Reuters reports Starbucks lowered profit guidance while hiking prices to offset inflation [[n0593]].
EPS Upside Watch

Pricing is the lever. CNBC reports Amazon raised the price of Prime nearly 17% to $139 per year [[n0631]]. Companies with subscription or brand power can pass costs through; Starbucks, -14.52% over 20 sessions to 95.00 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), shows the cost of failing to do so fast enough.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Peloton, -27.35% over 20 sessions to 24.60 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), may now trade as a takeover story rather than a broken growth stock: the WSJ reports Amazon and other potential suitors are exploring a deal [[n0770]]. M&A optionality now outweighs standalone demand.
Narrative

Staples did their defensive job over 20 sessions but lagged the growth rally. XLP closed at 75.89 USD, -1.87% over 20 sessions against the S&P 500's -4.16%, yet only +0.28% over five sessions and -1.22% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), with Procter & Gamble -1.59% to 161.53 USD and PepsiCo -1.64% to 172.49 USD.
Reported

Barron's reports Clorox stock fell sharply as rising costs hit margins [[n1139]]. Hershey went the other way, forecasting annual profit above estimates as price hikes take effect, per Reuters [[n0668]], and Barron's says Costco saw another strong sales month though the stock did not leap [[n0646]]; Costco closed at 519.77 USD, +5.55% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04).
EPS Upside Watch

Brand strength separates the group: firms whose price increases stick can protect margins. Corn at 620.50 US cents/bu and soybeans at 1,553.50 US cents/bu, +12.80% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), keep ingredient costs elevated.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Business Insider quotes an ex-McDonald's CEO saying inflation is driving every restaurant absolutely crazy [[n1167]]. The contrarian read: staples with proven pricing power become growth substitutes if the economy slows while inflation stays high, so rate-day weakness in price-makers is an entry point.
Narrative

Health care is quietly working as the lower-beta quality hedge. XLV closed at 132.30 USD, +1.39% over five sessions and -2.03% over 20, far ahead of the Nasdaq 100's -6.79% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04).
Reported

Reuters reports AbbVie sees strong 2022 earnings as Botox and Skyrizi powered a profit beat [[n0497]], and Pharmaceutical Technology reports Lilly's full-year 2021 revenue rose 15% [[n1147]]. Results did not guarantee rewards: Barron's explains why Regeneron fell despite strong earnings [[n0112]], and Fierce Pharma says Biogen still expects minimal Aduhelm sales [[n0629]]. Lilly closed at 242.27 USD, -6.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04).
EPS Upside Watch

Fierce Pharma reports Gilead's COVID antiviral Veklury blew past sales estimates as Omicron surged [[n1051]], but that revenue fades with the wave. Pfizer's report, previewed by 24/7 Wall St. [[n0768]], is the next test of how much COVID revenue investors are willing to capitalise.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Moderna, -24.55% over 20 sessions to 163.01 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), won full US approval for its adult COVID vaccine, per Reuters [[n0345]]. Approval is no longer a catalyst; the market is pricing COVID franchises as wasting assets and paying instead for durable franchises such as AbbVie's.
Narrative

Materials are split between agricultural inputs and industrial metals. XLB closed at 83.12 USD, -1.66% on Friday and -7.00% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), but fertilizer names trade on geopolitics: Mosaic rose +10.21% over five sessions to 43.83 USD and CF Industries +5.57% to 75.06 USD.
Reported

Reuters reports Nutrien eyes a potash production boost amid turmoil in Russia and Belarus [[n0273]], and Corteva eyes annual sales above expectations on solid demand [[n0523]]. Alcoa rose +11.88% over five sessions to 64.22 USD, with aluminium at 3,114.25 USD/t, +7.76% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04).
EPS Upside Watch

Reuters reports electric vehicles are driving up nickel, cobalt and lithium prices [[n1876]], a structural tailwind for battery-metal suppliers. Farm Policy News says Russia-Ukraine tensions are unnerving grain markets [[n1342]], which supports fertilizer demand and pricing into the planting season.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Gold at 1,807.80 USD/oz is only +1.04% over 20 sessions despite war risk, while palladium is +22.33% to 2,287.40 USD/oz (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). The pattern suggests metals are pricing supply exposure to Russia rather than safe-haven demand, so bullion is a poor war hedge in this set-up.
Narrative

Real estate is the clearest casualty of the rate repricing. XLRE closed at 46.69 USD, -1.37% on Friday and -5.73% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), as the 10Y rose 20 bps over 20 observations to 1.93% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-04).
Reported

MONEY reports mortgage rates moved higher [[n2060]], and HousingWire says Santander Bank will stop originating mortgages in the United States [[n2056]]. Underlying demand remains firm: Forbes reports one-third of houses for sale are new construction, an all-time high [[n2030]], and the Joint Center for Housing Studies describes a record-breaking rental market [[n2033]].
EPS Upside Watch

Residential landlords can reprice rents faster than office or retail owners reprice leases, so funds from operations should hold up best in apartments and single-family rentals, where record rental demand persists.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Rate pain may be overstated for owners of scarce housing; Bloomberg suggests following the kids to see where the US housing boom still has legs [[n0225]]. The sector trades as a bond proxy, yet much of its rental income is effectively inflation-linked.
Narrative

Utilities are a weak defensive in a rising-yield, rising-fuel environment. XLU closed at 68.48 USD, -0.80% on Friday and -2.00% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), with Duke Energy -1.12% to 104.25 USD.
Reported

Exelon completed the separation of Constellation, per Business Wire [[n0539]], creating what Constellation calls the largest US clean energy company [[n0520]]. Customers face fuel pass-through: KRCR reports PG&E customers are seeing bills rise on natural gas prices [[n1788]], and Henry Hub stands at 4.57 USD/MMBtu, +19.94% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04).
EPS Upside Watch

NextEra rose +4.84% over five sessions to 76.01 USD and Enphase +14.02% to 141.23 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), suggesting renewables are being re-rated as energy security. Georgia Power's plan to double renewables and ditch all coal, per E&E News [[n0418]], expands the regulated rate base on which returns are earned.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Japan is the warning for gas-heavy generators: the Japan Times reports utilities reeling as sky-high fuel prices hit earnings [[n1059]]. Where regulators lag fuel costs, earnings fall even as revenue rises, so prefer renewables-heavy rate bases.
Narrative

European autos sold off on Friday. The SXAP tracker (EXV5.DE) closed at 59.27 EUR, -3.19% on the day and -8.36% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). BMW fell -4.37% to 89.66 EUR, Renault -3.98% to 34.29 EUR, VW preference shares -3.08% to 176.14 EUR and Mercedes-Benz Group -2.67% to 67.83 EUR.
Reported

Daimler formally became Mercedes-Benz Group, per Business Wire [[n0389]]. Reuters reports Volvo Cars' January sales tumbled as the chip shortage lingered [[n1870]], and the BBC says Jaguar Land Rover lost £9m to the global chip shortage [[n1807]]. Automotive News reports Stellantis says suppliers bear all the risk [[n0819]]; Stellantis' US line fell -3.46% to 19.00 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04).
EPS Upside Watch

Reuters reports automakers and chip firms differ on when the semiconductor shortage will abate [[n1134]]. Volume recovery is the upside: CNBC reports GM forecasts earnings at or near record levels in 2022 as the chip shortage eases [[n0416]], and European peers need the same supply normalisation to deliver.
⚡ Breaking Convention

ACEA reports battery-electric cars took a 9.1% market share of new cars in 2021 [[n1851]]. The EV transition, not the chip shortage, is the longer-run margin risk for incumbents, because it forces heavy investment as pricing power peaks.
Narrative

Semiconductors bounced on results but remain in a 20-session drawdown. SOXX closed at 476.82 USD, +4.79% over five sessions and -11.18% over 20, and the PHLX Semiconductor Index at 3,453.07 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). ASML's US line is -14.46% over 20 sessions to 652.81 USD, while TSMC's ADR is only -5.80% to 121.02 USD.
Reported

CNBC reports AMD rose 10% after issuing a strong 2022 sales outlook [[n0360]]; it closed +17.45% over five sessions at 123.60 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). SK hynix reported fourth-quarter results [[n0987]] and rose +5.51% over five sessions to 124,500.00 KRW. Bloomberg reports chipmakers tumbled amid a high bar for Qualcomm's earnings [[n0643]], yet Qualcomm closed +7.59% over five sessions.
EPS Upside Watch

BofA's Arya tells CNBC AMD earnings could potentially double or triple over the next few years [[n1080]]. Capacity investment continues at the specialist end: Reuters reports Toshiba will invest $1 billion to double power chip production [[n1456]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Equipment is the overlooked laggard: Lam Research is -17.50% over 20 sessions while Tokyo Electron gained +5.80% last week (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Axios warns the next microchip crisis will be bigger [[n1795]], which argues for buying capacity suppliers on weakness.

earnings_pattern.title: Pricing power and data scale paid; visibility gaps punished
parts: Rewarded

Investors paid for growth backed by visible pricing. Amazon rose +13.54% to 3,152.79 USD, Snap +58.82% to 38.91 USD and Pinterest +11.18% to 27.25 USD on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Reuters reports Pinterest's results dazzled Wall Street as its ad business boomed [[n0703]], and TechCrunch's verdict was simply that Snap finally did it [[n1121]]. Alphabet's 20-for-1 stock split, announced with results per CNBC [[n0422]], added a retail-access angle to a beat.
Punished

Guidance and user metrics were punished without mercy. Reuters reports Meta shares sank 20% as Facebook lost daily users for the first time [[n0565]], and Meta Platforms (FB) is -28.69% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). PayPal is -22.90% over five sessions to 126.08 USD after Forbes reported a crash that wiped out over $50 billion in value when it lowered its profit outlook [[n0577]]. Ford fell -9.70% despite its outlook, and Reuters reports Spotify sank on weaker-than-expected first-quarter subscriber numbers [[n0592]].
Pattern

The common thread is control over the customer. Companies that own the platform or the price, such as Amazon with Prime fees and Alphabet with search data, were rewarded; companies dependent on others' platforms or facing user churn were de-rated. CNBC notes Facebook and Google stocks diverged, and the reason is Apple [[n0656]]. In a rising-rate market the penalty for a guidance cut is larger, because the long-dated cash flows that justify growth multiples are discounted harder.
Attention into EPS

Attention shifts to energy, pharma and the gig economy: 24/7 Wall St. previews BP, Pfizer and Sysco [[n0768]], and ig.com sets out what to expect from Uber's Q4 2021 results [[n0087]]. Uber rose +7.27% on Friday to 37.05 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), so the bar is already higher. BP, +11.96% over 20 sessions to 405.90 GBp, will be judged against the Shell and Exxon template of rising payouts.
Playbook

Buy beats that come with guidance raises or price increases; fade beats that rely on one-off gains, such as Ford's 2021 profit, which the New York Times says was bolstered by a large gain on its Rivian stake [[n0660]]. Amazon also booked a Rivian gain, but the market paid for AWS and Prime pricing. Trigger: a stock holding most of its first-day reaction for a week signals institutional sponsorship. What changes the call: a macro shock that compresses all multiples, making dispersion secondary to net exposure.

underowned.title: Fertilizers: the Russia-Belarus supply premium
parts: Attention Gap

Ukraine coverage centres on oil and gas, but potash and nitrogen are just as exposed to Russia and Belarus. Reuters reports Nutrien eyes a potash production boost amid turmoil in both countries [[n0273]], and pb.pl surveys the outlook for fertilizer prices [[n1723]].
Exposure & Risk

Mosaic (MOS) closed at 43.83 USD, +11.22% over 20 sessions, Nutrien (NTR) at 72.41 USD and CF Industries (CF) at 75.06 USD, +8.41% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). The risks are demand destruction if farmers cut application rates and a diplomatic settlement that removes the supply premium.
Trigger to Watch

Grain prices. AgWeb reports the threat of war is rattling grain markets and driving wheat prices higher [[n1808]]; CBOT wheat at 763.25 US cents/bu, +2.31% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), pushing higher would confirm the fertilizer bid.

underowned.title: Uranium and nuclear: baseload after the clean-tech sell-off
parts: Attention Gap

Bloomberg reports volatility raging in uranium stocks as clean tech takes a beating [[n0478]], while the WSJ profiles a new company betting big on nuclear power in America [[n0598]]. The group is being sold alongside growth rather than analysed on its own supply-demand balance.
Exposure & Risk

Cameco (CCJ) closed at 19.89 USD, +4.03% on Friday but -12.46% over 20 sessions; the URA ETF at 20.51 USD and Centrus Energy (LEU) at 42.15 USD, -13.57% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Liquidity is thin, moves are violent and policy support can reverse with elections.
Trigger to Watch

Contracting and policy momentum. Reuters reports China inked an $8 bln nuclear power plant deal in Argentina [[n1845]], and Constellation's launch as the largest US clean energy company [[n0520]] gives investors a large listed nuclear operator to price the theme.

underowned.title: Defence primes: eastern-flank spending
parts: Attention Gap

Troop movements dominate the news; procurement budgets are the slower, larger story. Reuters reports Germany is eyeing the Lockheed F-35, with no final decision [[n0665]], and the Japan Times argues economic security in Japan needs to include the defence industry [[n1447]].
Exposure & Risk

Lockheed Martin (LMT) closed at 389.33 USD, +8.75% over 20 sessions, Raytheon Technologies (RTX) at 93.01 USD, +3.28%, and Rheinmetall (RHM.DE) at 90.52 EUR, +3.71%, while the ITA ETF is -2.96% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). A diplomatic settlement could unwind the premium quickly, and Reuters reports Boeing says Ukraine tensions are creating an adverse climate for business [[n0268]].
Trigger to Watch

Procurement decisions. A German F-35 order or further eastern-flank deployments beyond the 1,700 troops Notes From Poland reports heading to Poland [[n1501]] would convert rhetoric into multi-year orders for the primes.

underowned.title: China EV ADRs: the post-holiday catch-up
parts: Attention Gap

Chinese EV makers are discussed as Tesla challengers, rarely as the purest listed play on Beijing's easing. CNBC reports Xpeng delivered over 10,000 cars for a fifth straight month [[n0379]], and CnEVPost's finding that China took 53% of global passenger NEV sales in 2021 [[n0244]] shows the scale.
Exposure & Risk

Li Auto (LI) closed at 28.70 USD, +19.73% over five sessions, while XPeng (XPEV) at 37.25 USD is -20.17% over 20 and NIO at 23.96 USD is -18.25% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Battery-metal inflation and price competition squeeze margins, and US-China friction adds tail risk.
Trigger to Watch
Mainland reopening. If onshore shares catch up with Hong Kong's +3.24% post-holiday gain and monthly deliveries hold up, the EV names are the highest-beta beneficiaries of the policy turn.

crypto.title: Bitcoin rebounds with tech beta; hacks and tax rules cap it
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 42,412.43 USD, +2.34% on the day, +9.47% over five sessions and only +0.38% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-06), so Bitcoin has only climbed back to where it stood 20 sessions ago. Ether closed at 3,057.48 USD, +9.50% over five sessions but -4.82% over 20, and Solana at 115.30 USD is still -17.60% over 20. Forbes Middle East reports a market rebound with Bitcoin rising above $40,500 [[n0948]]. The move coincided with Friday's growth rally: MicroStrategy rose +15.16% to 391.64 USD, GBTC +13.52% to 25.26 USD and Coinbase +7.24% to 194.44 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04).
New / Most Important

Plumbing risk resurfaced. CNBC reports more than $320 million was stolen in the latest apparent crypto hack [[n0923]], and The Defiant says Jump Crypto replaced over $320M of Wormhole wrapped ETH in a DeFi bailout [[n0936]]; a private backstop contained contagion this time, but not by design. Regulation is tightening at the edges: Reuters reports India will tax cryptocurrencies at 30% [[n0905]], Bloomberg says Russia values local crypto at $200 billion as rules near [[n0909]], and the BBC reports a UN finding that North Korea's missile programme was funded through stolen crypto [[n1413]]. Capital is still arriving, with CNBC reporting FTX hit a $32 billion valuation despite bear-market fears [[n0283]].
Playbook

Action: treat crypto as high-beta technology, not a hedge; keep core Bitcoin exposure small and avoid leveraged miners into the next CPI print. Trigger to add: Bitcoin holding above 42,250.55 USD, its close 20 sessions earlier, while the 2Y keeps rising would show genuine decoupling from rates. What changes the call: Al Jazeera reports Bitcoin jumped 10% past $40,000 for the first time in 2 weeks [[n0945]]; a daily close back below $40,000 would signal the rebound has failed, and another bridge exploit would argue for cutting DeFi exposure first.

flows.title: Liquidity drains at the front end while credit leaks
parts: Global Liquidity

Developed-market liquidity is tightening on three fronts. CNBC reports the Federal Reserve pointed to a rate hike coming in March [[n2089]], with Bullard arguing for three successive hikes [[n2104]]; the Bank of England's base rate rose to 0.5%, per Money Saving Expert [[n1239]], and Reuters explains how the BoE plans to reverse QE by giving up gilts [[n1220]]; and Lagarde is no longer ruling out an ECB hike this year [[n0100]]. The Economist warns the global interest bill is about to jump [[n0239]]. The Washington Post reports inflation has Fed critics pointing to the spike in money supply [[n2148]], the excess liquidity that tightening must now absorb. The counter-current is China, where the central bank is adding stimulus. Net, liquidity is being withdrawn faster than Beijing adds it, which favours assets with near-term cash flows over those priced on distant ones.
Rates & Dollar

The repricing is concentrated at the front end: the 2Y rose 43 bps over 20 observations to 1.31% against 20 bps for the 10Y at 1.93%, a bear flattening that leaves 10Y-2Y moderately steep at +62 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-04). Bond ETFs show the duration loss, with TLT -2.88% over five sessions to 139.01 USD and IEF -1.22% to 111.20 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Supply helps the long end: Gulf Times reports the US Treasury cut its quarterly sale of long-term debt [[n0114]], which helps explain why the 10Y lagged the 2Y. The dollar index (DXY) nevertheless fell -1.84% over five sessions to 95.48 index points as hawkish ECB and BoE signals narrowed the policy gap; Reuters had flagged the dollar's rally may have seen a short-term peak [[n0018]]. A softer DXY eases pressure on emerging markets, but Reuters' dashboard of EM vulnerabilities to rising global rates [[n1308]] shows the relief is conditional.
Credit Check

Credit is leaking, not breaking. Reuters reports US high-yield bond ETFs saw record outflows in January [[n1296]]. HYG is -2.69% over 20 sessions to 83.77 USD, while LQD is -3.71% to 125.45 USD, losing more than junk because of its longer duration (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Reuters notes tech-light corporate bonds have swerved the worst of the stock market's woes [[n1228]], so the stress is rate-driven rather than default-driven, and Reuters reports Carlyle is in talks to acquire credit investment firm CBAM [[n0761]], a sign private capital still wants credit platforms. EMB, the dollar EM bond ETF, is -2.28% over 20 sessions to 104.35 USD. The Times of Malta looks beneath the bonnet of high yield [[n1310]]; the pattern argues for shortening credit duration rather than cutting credit risk outright.
Equity & Fund Flows

Equity money is rotating within markets more than leaving them. Bloomberg reports Meta's drop could hit stock funds with $1 trillion that bet on the Facebook parent [[n0684]], a concentration risk for index and growth funds alike. Corporate cash is the steadiest buyer: Exxon's $10 billion repurchase [[n1291]] and Shell's higher buybacks, per CNBC [[n0700]], recycle commodity windfalls into equity. Hedge-fund results map the rotation: Bloomberg reports AQR's absolute return fund had a record month with a 15.4% return [[n1841]], and Discovery Capital gained 4% in January on the market's value move [[n1858]]. Robinhood rose +19.25% over five sessions to 15.18 USD and ARKK +5.57% to 72.75 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), a speculative bounce rather than a regime change given ARKK is still -14.99% over 20 sessions.
Portfolio Implication

Position for tighter liquidity with selective risk: keep duration short, hold quality and value equities (energy, money-centre banks, cash-generative platforms), and underweight long-duration growth and long-maturity investment-grade credit. Trigger: further bear flattening with the 2Y at or above 1.31% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-04), and HYG failing to recover its 20-session loss of -2.69% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), keeps the stance. What changes the call: a credit-led sell-off, visible as high yield underperforming investment grade, would shift the problem from rates to growth and argue for adding Treasury duration even as the Fed starts hiking.

anticipatory.title: The next US CPI print and the size of lift-off
parts: What Is Priced

CNBC reports the Fed pointed to a hike in March [[n2089]], so the debate is size. December inflation rose 7%, the highest since 1982, per CNBC [[n1961]], and the 2Y at 1.31% has risen 43 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-04). CME Group lays out rate-hike expectations against reality [[n2114]], while Reuters argues a big-bang start is not likely [[n2139]].
Conditional Expression

If the next CPI print runs hot, the cleanest expression is further front-end weakness and a flatter curve: stay short the 2Y and long XLF against XLRE. If it surprises softer, the bear flattening should unwind first at the 2Y, favouring a tactical rebound in the Nasdaq 100, still -6.79% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), and in rate-sensitive real estate.
Risk

Inflation is not the only driver. A geopolitical shock could pull yields down even with a hot print, turning a short-duration position into a loser. Wages are the persistence test; Apricitas Economics asks what is going on with wages [[n2135]], and a fast wage trend would keep the Fed hawkish whatever the monthly CPI does.

anticipatory.title: Russia-Ukraine: diplomacy against a pending invasion risk
parts: What Is Priced

Oil and gas carry the premium; equities carry little. Brent is +13.76% over 20 sessions to 93.27 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), and Reuters reports strategists see oil hitting $100 [[n1389]]. NBC reports nerves fraying at the Ukraine border as Russian troops mass in Belarus [[n1411]], and the Economist says America is preparing the mother of all sanctions [[n1404]].
Conditional Expression

POLITICO reports Macron heading east on a risky peacemaker mission [[n1280]]. If diplomacy gains traction, fade the oil premium through energy against the market and add European cyclicals such as autos, with the SXAP tracker -8.36% over 20 sessions at 59.27 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). If invasion risk escalates, own energy, defence and Treasuries, and cut Polish and euro-area banks.
Risk

Sanctions may spare energy flows. The Japan Times notes Putin's financial fortress blunts the impact of threatened sanctions [[n1391]], so even an escalation might not deliver the physical supply shock oil is pricing, leaving long-energy positions exposed to a sharp reversal.

anticipatory.title: Poland's February MPC decision
parts: What Is Priced

Pekao expects the Monetary Policy Council to raise rates by 50 bps in February [[n1706]], and bank shares already reflect higher rates, with Pekao +8.56% over 20 sessions at 134.40 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Money.pl notes Czech rates are twice as high as Poland's [[n1683]], a gap that keeps pressure on the NBP to catch up.
Conditional Expression

A hike in line with Pekao's call keeps the bank overweight intact. A larger move or hawkish guidance would favour PKO BP and mBank further and could stabilise the zloty, which helps importers such as LPP. A smaller move would hit the currency and the banks together, the worst outcome for Polish exposure.
Risk

Business Insider Polska argues a clear fall in inflation is entirely in Glapiński's hands [[n1582]]. If the NBP under-delivers, inflation expectations rise, real rates fall further, and the bank trade becomes a currency trade that foreign holders can exit quickly.

anticipatory.title: China's reopening and the next easing step
parts: What Is Priced

Hong Kong has priced a policy-led recovery. The Hang Seng rose +3.24% on reopening and Tencent is +9.67% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), while the Shanghai Composite's last close of 3,361.44 index points still reflects the -7.12% pre-holiday slide (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-28).
Conditional Expression

If mainland shares open firm and the central bank adds easing, ASHR, at 36.53 USD and -3.79% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), is the catch-up trade against FXI. If the services survey disappoints or property news worsens, Hong Kong's gains are vulnerable and Australian miners such as Fortescue, +9.72% over five sessions to 21.34 AUD, would give back their China premium.
Risk

Zero-COVID cuts both ways: the New York Times reports China's strict virus policy has left fruit abandoned [[n0235]], a reminder that lockdowns hit supply and consumption together. The Asia Times frames an Olympian Soros-versus-Dalio debate on China [[n0230]]; with positioning this split, a disappointment could move prices sharply.

catalysts.title: Meta Platforms (FB)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Meta Platforms (FB) closed at 237.09 USD, -21.42% over five sessions and -28.69% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). CNBC reports Facebook says Apple's iOS privacy change will mean a $10 billion revenue hit this year [[n0540]], and CNBC says the metaverse business lost more than $10 billion last year, with losses still growing [[n1061]]. The thesis: a de-rating from compounder to capital-intensive turnaround.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Recovery needs stable daily users; Business Insider reports Zuckerberg citing unprecedented competition from TikTok [[n1127]]. The risk to the bearish stance is valuation: Business Insider notes Meta sank below Berkshire Hathaway in market value for the first time in nearly two years [[n0688]], inviting value buyers.
Trade Expression
Stay underweight; prefer Alphabet for advertising exposure. Revisit only if measurement fixes restore ad pricing and the stock holds above 237.09 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04).

catalysts.title: Amazon (AMZN)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Amazon closed at 3,152.79 USD, +13.54% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), a jump Bloomberg calls a record $191 billion gain in market value [[n0107]]. GeekWire reports Amazon would have posted a $1.8 billion Q4 operating loss without AWS [[n0635]], and CNBC sizes its advertising business at $31 billion a year [[n1088]]. The thesis: three high-margin engines, cloud, ads and Prime pricing, now fund retail.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The 20-session change is still -3.44% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), so the stock has only partly recovered its January loss. Reuters cites rising wages and costs behind the Prime fee hike [[n1089]], and Bloomberg says a Peloton deal may pose a regulatory headache for a tech giant [[n0866]].
Trade Expression
Own, and add if the stock holds most of Friday's +13.54% gain through the week. Exit if AWS growth decelerates or Prime churn rises.

catalysts.title: Exxon Mobil (XOM)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Exxon closed at 81.41 USD, +8.14% over five sessions and +19.16% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). The New York Times reports an $8.9 billion fourth-quarter profit as oil prices soared [[n0402]], MarketWatch says Exxon will merge chemicals and refining in a cost-cutting reorganisation [[n0405]], and World Oil reports it joining Chevron in a Permian surge [[n1010]]. The thesis: cash returns plus volume growth.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Brent at 93.27 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04) already discounts much of the war premium. Reuters reports the US restored a sanctions waiver to Iran with nuclear talks in a final phase [[n1398]]; a deal, or Ukraine de-escalation, would cut the price that funds buybacks.
Trade Expression
Hold core and add on pullbacks while WTI keeps its +16.17% 20-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04); reduce if Brent loses its +13.76%.

catalysts.title: PayPal (PYPL)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

PayPal closed at 126.08 USD, -22.90% over five sessions and -34.43% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Payments Dive reports PayPal scrapped its account growth goal [[n0579]], and Forbes says it admitted 4.5 million accounts were illegitimate as fintech's fraud problem grows [[n1068]]. The thesis: user growth, the core of the valuation, has stalled.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The bear case is now consensus, and Wolfe Research's Darrin Peller tells CNBC he believes there will be consistency to PayPal's growth [[n0482]]. Any stabilising engagement metric could force a sharp short-covering rally from depressed levels.
Trade Expression

Avoid; prefer Visa, 228.39 USD and +3.93% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), for payments exposure. Revisit only if management restores a credible account target and engagement stabilises.

catalysts.title: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

AMD closed at 123.60 USD, +17.45% over five sessions but -9.27% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). CNBC reports CEO Lisa Su says AMD grew in every business [[n1036]], and Notebookcheck says AMD expects record 2022 earnings and is closing in on Intel's profit margins [[n1037]]. The thesis is continuing share gains against a stumbling incumbent.
Price Hurdle & Risk
